claims.statement: desktop/ is an additive Tauri v2 shell that implements no backend logic of its own: it spawns the ordinary `oxyromon` binary as a sidecar running `server --address 127.0.0.1 --port <port>` and points the webview at it, so the SPA, GraphQL API, uploads, downloads, database and settings are all reused unchanged from the CLI's server build.

desktop/Cargo.toml declares its own empty [workspace] and publish = false so tauri and tauri-plugin-shell (its only dependencies) and the platform webview stay out of the CLI build; as a standalone crate it carries its own size-oriented [profile.release] (opt-level "z", lto, codegen-units 1, strip) independent of the root profile.

The loopback port is reserved by binding 127.0.0.1:0 and reading back the assigned port; the listener is dropped before the sidecar binds it, which the code documents as a small reuse race whose only consequence is a failed readiness check.

Startup blocks on readiness by polling TcpStream::connect to 127.0.0.1:<port> every 50 ms for up to 30 seconds; on timeout server::start returns an error naming the port and deadline, and no window is opened.
desktop/src/main.rs runs sidecar startup synchronously inside the Tauri setup hook, so the child is spawned and confirmed listening before the 1400x900 (minimum 800x600) webview is built.

Because the window is loaded via WebviewUrl::External from the sidecar's own http://127.0.0.1:<port> origin, the Leptos SPA keeps using same-origin relative URLs (/graphql, /events, /dats, /romfiles/{id}), so no CORS handling and no desktop-specific frontend build are needed; desktop/capabilities/default.json accordingly grants an empty permission set to the "main" window and tauri.conf.json sets withGlobalTauri false and csp null.

desktop/scripts/stage-sidecar.sh resolves the repository root from its own location and the target triple from TARGET_TRIPLE or `rustc -vV`, runs `cargo build --release --features server` from the repo root, and copies the result to desktop/binaries/oxyromon-<triple>[.exe] — the triple-suffixed name Tauri requires for the externalBin entry ["binaries/oxyromon"]; beforeDevCommand and beforeBuildCommand both invoke it.

Because staging builds with the `server` feature, the desktop toolchain includes the web UI toolchain: root build.rs runs `trunk build --release` unless SKIP_TRUNK=true, so trunk and the wasm32-unknown-unknown target are prerequisites for any desktop build.

desktop/build.rs calls tauri_build::build(), which makes the staged sidecar a build-time requirement: a plain `cargo build` in desktop/ fails until desktop/binaries/oxyromon-<triple> exists. binaries/, gen/ and target/ are generated and gitignored.

The sidecar's CommandChild is stored in Tauri managed state as Server(Mutex<Option<CommandChild>>) immediately after spawn and before the readiness wait; Server::shutdown() take()s the slot and kill()s the child, making it idempotent, and main.rs invokes it on RunEvent::Exit because the sidecar is not in the shell's process group and would otherwise be orphaned holding the database.

Sidecar stdout, stderr, CommandEvent::Error and CommandEvent::Terminated are drained by a spawned async task and re-emitted on the desktop process's stderr with an `[oxyromon]` prefix, giving the only diagnostic channel for server startup failures.

The desktop sidecar is the ordinary oxyromon binary and resolves its database the same way as the CLI — config::get_data_directory, which is OXYROMON_DATA_DIRECTORY, else the platform data directory, plus oxyromon.db — so the desktop app and the CLI share one database, one set of settings and one set of imported Wii U keys.

Since the sidecar is built with `server`, its pool uses max_connections 5 and PRAGMA locking_mode = NORMAL with WAL instead of the headless build's single EXCLUSIVE connection, which is what lets the desktop's long-lived server coexist with CLI invocations on the same database file.

The desktop bundle is host-only: dist.sh builds it once after the whole cross matrix with NO_STRIP=true and copies the resulting .deb, .rpm and .AppImage into dist/, because Tauri links the platform's own webview and no cross toolchain exists for it; desktop.sh is the standalone equivalent.

Recorded failure modes: a blank window on Linux is WebKitGTK's DMA-BUF renderer on some GPU/driver combinations (confirm with WEBKIT_DISABLE_DMABUF_RENDERER=1); `failed to locate the bundled oxyromon binary` means the sidecar was never staged for the current target triple; and `failed to run linuxdeploy` is linuxdeploy's too-old binutils failing on .relr.dyn sections, worked around with NO_STRIP=true.

CI never validates the desktop crate: the single CI workflow pins SKIP_TRUNK=true workflow-wide and builds the web UI once in its `Build web UI` step (`cd frontend && trunk build --release`, trunk pinned by TRUNK_VERSION) so the clippy/build/llvm-cov `--workspace` steps reuse those assets, and since desktop/ declares its own [workspace] while the root workspace members are only crates/* and the only separate-workspace clippy pass targets frontend/, no CI step ever compiles the shell or installs the Tauri CLI or webkit2gtk — regressions there surface only in a manual or dist.sh build.

The child-kill path is reachable only through the Tauri run loop: if setup fails after the spawn (e.g. the readiness timeout), main's expect on building the app aborts before app.run, so nothing in this code reaps the already-spawned sidecar.

tauri.conf.json declares no static windows and registers tauri-plugin-shell only so Rust code can call app.shell().sidecar(...); combined with the empty capability permission set, page scripts get no Tauri IPC, shell or process surface at all.

The desktop runtime needs no external format tools: every format is served by in-tree crates or Rust dependencies (chd-rs, cia-rs, xso-rs, gdi-rs, xdelta-rs, xps-rs, nsz-rs, wux-rs, sevenz-rust2/zip, nod), which `src/info.rs` reports as built-in versions, so no external binary is needed for any format.

Because those dependencies moved in tree, the desktop bundle declares no external-tool runtime dependency at all: tauri.conf.json has no bundle.linux.deb.depends table, so the Debian package's former p7zip dependency is gone (recorded in the 0.25.0 changelog), and the Alpine container likewise installs no codec or archive tool to run the server, removing its build-only packages after the build.

dist.sh's release matrix emits nine binaries per target — the server-enabled oxyromon plus the eight format-crate CLIs (chdrs, ciars, gdirs, nszrs, wuxrs, xdeltars, xpsrs, xsors) built with `cross build --release -p chd-rs -p cia-rs -p gdi-rs -p nsz-rs -p xdelta-rs -p wux-rs -p xps-rs -p xso-rs` — packed as .tar.xz (7z on windows gnullvm) and rcodesign-signed on Apple targets, before the host-only desktop bundle is appended to dist/.

dist.sh exports SKIP_TRUNK=true for the entire release run and Cross.toml passes that variable through to the cross images, so each target build embeds the host-built target/assets from the loop's own `trunk build --release` instead of rebuilding the wasm; the desktop staging build inherits the same value.
